chunks: And from him, from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Ibn Abi Yafur, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

He said: "The land tax (jizya) is not lifted from them [the people of the land], and indeed the jizya is the provision (ata') for the Muhajirun, and the zakat is for its specific people whom Allah named in His Book, and they have no share from the jizya."

Then he said: "How vast is justice!" Then he said: "Indeed, people become self-sufficient when justice is established among them, and the sky will send down its provision, and the earth will bring forth its blessings, by the permission of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic."
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between jizya and zakat in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes the fiscal nature of *jizya* as a provision (*ata'*) for the Muhajirun from *zakat*, which is strictly reserved for the eight categories specified in the Quran. He links this jurisprudential precision to a broader theological principle, asserting that equitable distribution of wealth fosters economic self-sufficiency and triggers divine blessings (*barakah*) in the skies and earth, a concept deeply rooted in Shia political economy.
